questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
He did prefer the 3335s over the 1907s in 2022, but by September 2023 he hedged: he says the 3335s "still might be" his favourite Red Wings, "but they probably not" [1], and he was selling them anyway.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):** He says he is on record calling the 3335s his favourite Red Wings of all time. He now hedges that. The 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1]. He still likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimbler feel, and says they are a little easier to go walking or take on a light hike in. Even so, "they're going" [1].

**Earlier view (Oct 2022):** He called the 3335s his favourite boots he has ever had and said they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [2]. His reasoning was that heritage work boots are made for work, and he is hiking and walking in the woods instead. He called the 3335s a dramatically better all-around boot [2]. He added that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily built, so someone who needs a tough boot probably shouldn't pick the 3335s [2].

He also said he doesn't think stitch-down gives the 3335s much of an edge over Goodyear-welted boots like the 1907 [3].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, the most recent video available, he is still a big fan of Blundstones, but he is retiring his own 585s to make room for other boots, not because they let him down.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):**
- He calls the 585s the boots from his first ever video, says he has worn them constantly, and says they have held up and stayed his most water-resistant boots. [1]
- He says "bluntstones are just incredible," that he's a big fan and has always loved them, though he notes some people really don't like them. [1]
- Even so, he decides it's "time to retire" them as part of cutting down his boot collection. [1]
- He also treats slip-ons like Blundstones as ones he can flop on quickly for errands or rain. He's keeping a slip-on pair for now but says it could easily go on the sell list. [2]
- He is letting go of his heavy-duty Blundstone work boots, which he found to be only very water-resistant nubuck, not waterproof as he had assumed. [3]

**How his view developed:**
- In 2019 he called them his favourite boots of the three or four he had. He recommended them if you keep them treated, and his main gripe was that the cemented soles can't technically be replaced. [4][5]
- In 2020, after a year untreated, he said they still looked great and were still great boots. He added that he would have picked a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck, and that they are decent but not exceptional as work boots. [6][7][8]

**Overall:** his lean is very positive, and the retirement is a collection cull, not a verdict against the boots.

questions.question: I'm wondering if you still have these boots and how are they holding up??? [Blundstones]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** As of his September 2023 boot-collection video, he was retiring his Blundstone 585s, the pair from his first video. He didn't say anything newer here about whether he still has them. He still thinks they held up very well.

**Latest (2023):** He says "it's time to retire those bunnies" [1]. He still praises them: he has worn them constantly, the leather is beat up and shiny with old wax, but "they've held up through it all" [2]. He calls them "probably my most water resistant boots through it all" [3].

**Earlier check-ins:**
- **2022 (about two years in):** He restored the pair with Otterwax, using conditioner and oil on the cracked, dry leather and then a wax layer [4].
- **2020 (one year in):** He said they look great and perform as he'd hoped for the price [5]. He noted more scuffs than he expected and lining wearing away at the big toe [6]. He also said he would pick a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck if he did it again [7].

The videos available here don't say whether he has since sold or donated the 585s, or how they have fared since 2023.

hybrid.answer:
He thinks the 1907 is the better buy of the two, but the 875 is still a boot he likes. In 2021 he called the 1907 Red Wing's best moc toe and said to get it over the 875 [1][2]. His most recent mention (2023) only says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [3].

**Construction (the main difference)**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant, and says the welt leaves room for cork that molds to your foot [4][5].
- The 1907 adds a storm (Norwegian-style) welt, which he values highly [6]. He relays the popular view from Reddit that Red Wing's version is just another strip of leather stitched onto the welt. He says he isn't quite sure about that [7].

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875, but he argues that's not really true once you count the extras [8].
- It comes with a removable leather footbed, which he says is typically about $40 separately. The footbed can come out to help the boots dry [9].
- It also comes with leather laces, typically about $15 [10].

**What they share**
- In 2022 he groups them together with crepe soles, which he thinks will break down faster than the Vibram sole on the 3335 [11]. In the 2021 video he also says he doesn't really like the crepe soles [12].
- Both are more beefily constructed than the 3335, so he says to look at them if you need a tough boot [13]. His 2022 favorite was the 3335, over both the 1907 and the 875 [13].

**Waterproofing**
- In his standing-in-water test, one 1907 leaked almost immediately through the stitching and the other stayed dry. He blamed one bigger stitch hole or imperfect waxing. He had no doubt the boots would hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [14][15].
- He didn't test the 875 in that video, so he gives no side-by-side water result.

He hasn't covered other differences between the two, such as leather or fit, in the videos available here.
